# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: CSI cursor movement / erase / edit + ESC fixture  (issue #6, wave 3)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/csi_spec.txt   (spec-researcher output)
#
# Evidence file for the implementer and the critic. Same machine-readable layout as
# print_c0_spec.txt (### ID / size / step / cite / note / screen / cursor / pending_wrap /
# requests / scrollback), so tests/csi.rs and tests/vttest.rs can reuse its parse_fixture.
# Extra keys (flags:, needs:, source:) are ignored by that parser. Deferred vttest screens
# are written as `#>` comment lines and are NOT cases.
#
# HOW THE EXPECTED SCREENS WERE PRODUCED
#   Part 1 (sequence x edge rows): tools/model.py, an independent Python model of xterm
#   written from xterm's source (charproc.c CASE_*, cursor.c, util.c, tabs.c; read from
#   ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots master, header $XTermId charproc.c 1.2134), NOT from
#   tessera-grid. Where the grid differs from xterm the case carries `flags: grid-trap` and
#   the note says which way the row goes (always xterm, except the one decision row D-CBT).
#   Part 2 (vttest): byte streams captured from the real vttest 2.7 (20251205, Homebrew
#   bottle) driven under a pty (24x80, TERM=xterm, tools/capture.py); expected screens from
#   the same model fed those exact bytes, then cross-checked against tmux 3.x running the
#   same vttest in a real 80x24 emulator (tools/tmux_oracle.sh). 11 of the 12 in-scope screens
#   are identical to tmux; V2S2 (tab stops) cannot be compared because tmux captures a literal HT, so it is
#   checked by vttest's own invariant (the two lines it draws must be identical, and are).
#   Part 1 was also run through tmux (tools/tmux_rows.py): 250 of 301 rows identical; the 51 differences
#   are all tmux deviations from xterm (tmux's pending-wrap model, IL/DL not resetting the column, no
#   CSI ^ / I / b support, DA/DSR replies, 24-parameter limit) and each was checked against xterm's source.
#   Capture files: vttest_capture/m<menu>_<NN>.bin (raw) and .esc.txt (script escape syntax).
#   Echo: the pty echo of the Enter key (CR LF) is part of the stream a real terminal
#   sees and some screens depend on it (RI after the prompt), so it is kept; only the
#   echo of the menu digit ("8\r\n") at the very start of a menu is stripped (ESC[2J follows).
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES
#   xterm ctlseqs   https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html
#                   (CSI Ps A..Z / @ ` b d e f g r ..., ESC 7 8 D E H M c, ESC # 8)
#   xterm source    https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots (master)
#                   charproc.c CASE_CUU CUD CUF CUB CUP VPA HPA CNL CPL ED EL ECH ICH DCH IL DL
#                              SU SD TBC CBT CHT HTS IND NEL RI DECSC DECRC DECSTBM DECALN REP RIS,
#                              ReallyReset, use_default_value()/one_if_default()
#                   cursor.c   CursorSet CursorBack CursorForward CursorDown CursorUp xtermIndex
#                              RevIndex CarriageReturn CursorNextLine CursorPrevLine CursorSave2
#                              CursorRestoreFlags
#                   util.c     InsertLine DeleteLine InsertChar DeleteChar ClearRight ClearInLine
#                              ClearScreen do_erase_display do_erase_line do_erase_char xtermScroll RevScroll
#                   tabs.c     TabToNextStop TabToPrevStop TabClear TabZonk
#   DEC             https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/{IL,DL,ICH,DCH,ECH,DECSTBM,CBT,HPA}.html
#                   https://vt100.net/docs/vt100-ug/chapter3.html (3.3 control sequences)
#                   (DEC STD 070 is not online; xterm's own comments cite its pages D-19/D-20 for DECALN
#                    and 5-186..5-191 for DECSC/DECRC)
#   vttest          https://invisible-island.net/vttest/  main.c tst_movements(), tst_screen(),
#                   tst_insdel(); esc.c helpers (cup() = `ESC [ r ; c H`, hvp() = `f`, decaln() = `ESC # 8`)
#
# PARSER FACTS the implementer needs (probed against tessera-vt 0.1, vte-based)
#   CSI H            -> params [0]      CSI ;H -> [0,0]     CSI 5;H -> [5,0]    CSI ;5H -> [0,5]
#   0 and omitted are the same and both mean "default" (xterm use_default_value: <=0 -> default).
#   99999999999 and 65536 saturate to 65535 (same as xterm MAX_I_PARAM): never overflows u16 parse,
#   but `n + cursor` arithmetic in u16 must saturate or use u32/usize.
#   32 parameters are kept (ignore:false), the 33rd sets ignore:true.
#   A private marker (? > = <) arrives as an INTERMEDIATE byte: `CSI ? 7 h` -> intermediates [63].
#   Every intermediate-bearing CSI must be treated as a different function (SP q, ! p, $ p, " H ...).
#   C0 inside a CSI executes immediately as its own Action::Execute BEFORE the Csi action
#   (`ESC [ 2 BS C` -> Execute(8), Csi{[2],'C'}); ESC inside restarts; CAN/SUB abort and the final byte
#   then prints as text. Colon sub-parameters are flattened (`1:2` -> [1,2]).
#   `CSI T` and `CSI 0 T` are indistinguishable ([0]).  `CSI - 1 A` yields no Csi action at all.
#
# DECISIONS FOR THE MILESTONE LEAD (recommended option first)
#   D-REP   Which actions clear State::last_printed. xterm (charproc.c, end of the parse loop:
#           `if (sp->parsestate == sp->groundtable) sp->lastchar = thischar;` with thischar = -1
#           for everything but a printable) clears it after EVERY completed non-printing action:
#           any C0 in ground, any ESC, CSI (including REP itself and an unimplemented SGR), OSC, DCS.
#           Recommend that rule: in State::apply, `let last = self.last_printed.take()` for every
#           non-Print action and hand `last` to REP. Rows REP06..REP10. (Alacritty keeps the char
#           across cursor moves; xterm is the reference.) C0 inside a half-parsed CSI also clears
#           here (xterm does not: it is not in ground state); only observable as `A ESC[ BS 3b`, ignore.
#           `REP` repeats through the normal print path, so wrap, IRM and the pending-wrap rules apply.
#           xterm guards with CharWidth(lastchar) > 0: control characters never become last_printed.
#   D-CBT   CBT (CSI Z) when pending wrap is armed. xterm's TabToPrevStop never resets the wrap
#           flag, so the flag survives a move left (the next print then wraps from col 16: an xterm
#           quirk). Recommend clearing pending wrap whenever CBT moves the cursor (grid.tab_backward
#           does). Row CBT08 follows the recommendation. CHT/HT with no stop to move to keep pending
#           (same decision as print_c0_spec D1); grid.tab_forward clears pending, so guard it
#           (row CHT07).
#   D-STBM  DECSTBM with top >= bottom after defaults/clamping is IGNORED ENTIRELY by xterm (`if (bot
#           > top)`): region unchanged, cursor NOT homed, pending untouched. Grid::set_scroll_region
#           resets to full screen in that case, so csi.rs must test bot > top BEFORE calling it.
#           Defaults: top = param0 (0 -> 1), bottom = param1 if 0 < p <= rows else rows. Success
#           homes the cursor (DECOM off: (0,0)) and clears pending. Rows STBM01..STBM15.
#   D-IL    IL/DL inside the region also move the cursor to column 0 (util.c InsertLine/DeleteLine:
#           set_cur_col(left margin)); outside the region they do nothing at all, not even the column
#           and not the pending wrap. Grid::insert_lines/delete_lines leave the column alone (call
#           carriage_return only when the row is inside the region) and clear pending even for the
#           no-op case. Recommend: csi.rs checks the region itself (`grid.scroll_region().contains(row)`),
#           calls the grid op and then carriage_return(); accept the one divergence that a no-op IL
#           outside the region clears pending wrap (row IL11 documents xterm; mark it
#           "accepted divergence" if the grid cannot be changed this wave).
#   D-ED    ED 3 and ED/EL with an unknown mode are no-ops in xterm and must not clear pending wrap;
#           Grid::erase_in_display/erase_in_line always do. Dispatch unknown modes to nothing
#           (rows ED06, ED13, EL05). ED 3 on a screen with pending wrap armed also keeps it in xterm;
#           grid.erase_in_display(Scrollback) clears it: accepted divergence (not tested).
#   D-SD0   `CSI 0 T`: xterm treats it as mouse-tracking reset (no screen effect); vte makes it
#           identical to `CSI T`. Recommend SD 1 for both. `CSI ^` / `CSI 0 ^` is SD (0 -> 1).
#   D-RIS   ESC c: xterm clears saved lines, resets tabs, margins, DECAWM (on) and IRM (off) and
#           the saved cursor. Grid::reset keeps scrollback, so call clear_scrollback() after it and
#           reset Terminal.auto_wrap/insert_mode. Rows RIS01..RIS05.
#   D-DECALN Fill row by row (goto(row,0) then cols x put_char('E')) so no row gets the wrapped flag
#           (a single put_char loop sets wrapped on every row and the render shows a trailing `\`),
#           reset the scroll region, clear pending, reset the pen, end at (0,0). Rows DECALN01..05.
#   D-SC    DECSC/DECRC save and restore pending wrap (xterm CursorRestoreFlags: `do_wrap =
#           sc->wrap_flag` after CursorSet). Matches Grid::save_cursor (brief decision 2). The scroll
#           region and tab stops are not saved. DECOM/charsets arrive with #8.
#   D-HPR   Not in the issue list but implemented by xterm: HPR (`a`), VPR (`e`), SCOSC/SCORC
#           (`CSI s`/`CSI u`), SL/SR (`CSI Ps SP @`/`A`). The brief said ignore; UNK07 still pins SL/SR
#           "ignored". HPR/VPR (#93) and SCOSC/SCORC (#94) are implemented since: rows UNK13 and SC09
#           were rewritten to xterm's behaviour and the HPR, VPR and SCO rows at the end of part 1 pin
#           them (VPR is CursorSet: it clamps to the screen, not to the bottom margin like CUD).
#   D-COLON `CSI 1:2 H` is rejected by xterm but flattened to [1,2] by vte: unfixable in csi.rs. Row UNK18.
#   D-SB    xterm saves scrolled-off lines whenever the TOP margin is row 1, even with a short
#           bottom margin (xtermScroll: scroll_all_lines = top_marg == 0); Grid::scroll_up only keeps
#           history for a full-screen region. No row depends on it (no row sets a 1;N region); accept the grid.
#   D-WIDE  Wide characters (width 2) and combining marks: deferred to #4's width handling. EL/ECH/ICH/DCH
#           that cut a wide character in half are not covered here; REP of a wide char must repeat it
#           as wide (brief decision 1) but no row asserts it.
#
# ISSUE TEXT / BRIEF CORRECTIONS (verified)
#   1. vttest "menu 6 (edit sequences)": WRONG. In vttest 2.7 the main menu is 0 Exit, 1 cursor
#      movements, 2 screen features, 3 character sets, 4 double-sized characters, 5 keyboard,
#      6 TERMINAL REPORTS (ENQ, LNM, DSR, DA, DECREQTPARM; not drawing, answers via requests; out
#      of #6), 7 VT52, 8 "VT102 features (Insert/Delete Char/Line)" = ICH/DCH/IL/DL, 9 bugs,
#      10 reset, 11 non-VT100. The edit-sequence menu is 8; this fixture covers 8 (V8*), not 6.
#   2. "Menu 1 screens 1-3 required": menu 1 has six holdit() screens: 1 = 80-col frame, 2 = the
#      same in 132 columns (DECCOLM resize), 3 = autowrap demo at 80 cols (needs DECOM + DECSTBM),
#      4 = same at 132, 5 = cursor controls inside CSI, 6 = leading zeros. Drivable with #6 alone:
#      screens 1, 5, 6. Screen 3 needs DECOM (#8). Screens 2/4 need DECCOLM 132 (#8).
#   3. Grid::set_scroll_region(top,bottom) with top>=bottom resets the region; xterm ignores the
#      whole sequence (D-STBM). 4. IL/DL leave the column unchanged in the grid; xterm resets it to
#      column 0 (D-IL). 5. The brief's DECALN recipe (put_char over rows x cols) marks every row as
#      soft-wrapped (D-DECALN). 6. Brief decision 1 hedges on whether movement clears last_printed:
#      xterm clears it on every non-print action (D-REP). 7. CNL/CPL/CUU/CUD at region boundaries need
#      no grid change: Grid::cursor_up/down already implement xterm's "stop at the margin unless the
#      cursor started outside the region" rule (rows CUU10..CUD13, CNL10, CPL10).
#   8. vttest streams contain ESC[?3l/h (DECCOLM) which xterm treats as clear-screen+home+reset-margins;
#      #6 ignores it. For the in-scope screens this is harmless (each starts with ED 2 or DECALN);
#      verified by running both semantics in the model (tools/gen.py asserts equality).
#
# SCRIPT / STEP SYNTAX, SCREEN RENDERING: identical to print_c0_spec.txt (decode() escapes \xNN \r \n \t \\
#   \u{H}; `step: set auto_wrap|insert_mode true|false`; render with '|' after the cursor cell, trailing
#   blanks stripped, '\' appended on soft-wrapped rows). All Part 1 rows use ASCII fill text
#   `abcdefghij / klmnopqrst / ...` (a-z A-Z 0-9 in reading order) and end with an `X` at the cursor so
#   position, overwrite and pending wrap are all visible. Cursor is 0-based (row,col).
#   Part 2 needs no harness change: vttest's ESC[?7h/l and ESC[4h/l are translated into the existing
#   `set auto_wrap` / `set insert_mode` steps (the only modes #6 scripts can toggle); every other byte
#   is verbatim from the capture.
# =============================================================================


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- PART 1
# PART 1: one case per sequence x parameter edge. Expected screens come from
# tools/model.py (an independent xterm-semantics model written from charproc.c,
# cursor.c, util.c, tabs.c; NOT from tessera-grid).

# ---------------------------------------- CUP

### CUP01_no_params
size: 5x10
step: feed \x1b[1;1Habcdefghij\x1b[2;1Hklmnopqrst\x1b[3;1HuvwxyzABCD\x1b[4;1HEFGHIJKLMN\x1b[5;1HOPQRSTUVWX
step: feed \x1b[3;5H\x1b[HX
cite: https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html CSI Ps ; Ps H (CUP) default [1,1]; https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/charproc.c CASE_CUP: CursorSet(one_if_default(0)-1, one_if_default(1)-1) clamps to the screen (cursor.c CursorSet)
note: CSI H homes: both parameters default to 1. vte delivers params=[0]; 0 means default (use_default_value: result<=0 -> default).
screen:
>Xb|cdefghij
>klmnopqrst
>uvwxyzABCD
>EFGHIJKLMN
>OPQRSTUVWX
cursor: (0,1)   # 1-based row 1 col 2
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0

### CUP12_extra_params_ignored
size: 5x10

### CBT08_pending_wrap

note: Pending armed at col 19. xterm's TabToPrevStop never calls ResetWrap, so in xterm the flag SURVIVES the move to col 16 and X wraps to row 2 (quirk). RECOMMENDED: CBT clears the pending wrap whenever it moves the cursor (grid.tab_backward does), so X lands at (0,16). The expected screen follows the RECOMMENDED behaviour. Decision D-CBT.

### SCO06_scorc_with_param_ignored
size: 5x10
step: feed \x1b[2;4H\x1b[s\x1b[4;8H\x1b[1uX
cite: https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html CSI s (SCOSC, only when DECLRMM is off), CSI u (SCORC); https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/charproc.c CASE_ANSI_SC (only_default() -> CursorSave), CASE_ANSI_RC (only_default(), falls through to CASE_DECRC -> CursorRestore); esctest2 esctest/tests/scorc.py
note: CSI 1 u is not only_default(): ignored, X at (3,7).
deviation: xterm's CASE_ANSI_RC breaks out WITHOUT ResetState, so its parser stays in the CSI state with the old parameters and takes the next byte as another final: in xterm `CSI 1 u X` runs ECH 1 at (3,7) and prints nothing. Tessera returns to ground after every sequence, so X prints; the row pins that.
screen:
>
>
>
>       X |
>
cursor: (3,8)   # 1-based row 4 col 9
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0

### SCO07_kitty_keyboard_queries_are_not_scorc
size: 5x10
step: feed \x1b[2;4H\x1b[s\x1b[4;8H\x1b[?u\x1b[>1u\x1b[<u\x1b[=1;1uX
cite: https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html CSI s (SCOSC, only when DECLRMM is off), CSI u (SCORC); https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/charproc.c CASE_ANSI_SC (only_default() -> CursorSave), CASE_ANSI_RC (only_default(), falls through to CASE_DECRC -> CursorRestore); esctest2 esctest/tests/scorc.py; https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/ (CSI ? u, CSI > flags u, CSI < u, CSI = flags ; mode u)
note: The kitty keyboard protocol's u sequences carry a private marker and never restore the cursor; X at (3,7).
screen:
>
>
>
>       X |
>
cursor: (3,8)   # 1-based row 4 col 9
pending_wrap: false

scrollback: len=0

### SCO08_explicit_zero_saves
size: 5x10
step: feed \x1b[2;4H\x1b[0s\x1b[4;8H\x1b[0uX
cite: https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html CSI s (SCOSC, only when DECLRMM is off), CSI u (SCORC); https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/charproc.c CASE_ANSI_SC (only_default() -> CursorSave), CASE_ANSI_RC (only_default(), falls through to CASE_DECRC -> CursorRestore); esctest2 esctest/tests/scorc.py
note: Tessera's parser reports CSI 0 s exactly like CSI s, so both save and restore: X at (1,3).
deviation: xterm stores an explicit 0 as 0, not DEFAULT, so only_default() fails: CSI 0 s is ignored, and CSI 0 u is ignored without ResetState (see SCO06), so X is taken as a CSI final (ECH 1 at (3,7)) and nothing prints; the cursor stays at (3,7). The parser cannot tell CSI 0 s from CSI s (same as D-SD0); the row pins Tessera's behaviour.
screen:
>
>   X |
>
>
>
cursor: (1,4)   # 1-based row 2 col 5
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- PART 2

# PART 2: vttest. Case ids V<menu>S<screen> map to the brief's snapshot names
#   vttest__menu<menu>_screen<screen> (screen = holdit() order within the menu, 1-based).
# IN SCOPE for #6 (drivable with #6 + `set auto_wrap` / `set insert_mode`):
#   menu 1: screens 1, 5, 6            menu 2: screens 1, 2, 12
#   menu 8 (pass 0, 80 columns): screens 1, 2 (ADAPTED), 3, 4, 5, 7
# Screens 3/4/5 of menu 8 depend on the state left by earlier screens, so their step lists are cumulative.
#
